title: AI Explainer Video Makers Compared [2026]
summary: Explainer video maker means two different products. Marketing explainers and comprehension explainers compared, with verified 2026 pricing and real timelines.
body_markdown:
Two people search **explainer video maker** in the same week and need opposite products. One wants a 90-second animated piece for a homepage, with characters, brand colors, and a script they already wrote. The other has a pull request they do not understand and wants somebody to walk them through it. Almost every roundup on this keyword ranks both kinds of tool in one list, which is how a person looking for an explanation ends up paying $699 a year for an animation suite.


Scrimba publishes this article and also makes one of the tools in the second category, so that is on the table from the start. This guide splits the two categories, compares inside each with pricing checked against the vendors' own plan pages in August 2026, and is straight about what each one costs, how long it takes, and where it fails.


## What Does "Explainer Video Maker" Actually Mean?


An explainer video maker is a tool that turns something you supply into a narrated video, and the whole category splits on what that something is: *a script you wrote* , or *a question you cannot answer* .


Those two inputs produce two unrelated products.


A **marketing explainer** is the familiar one. You already know what the video should say. The tool's job is production: characters, scenes, voiceover, brand styling, an exported file you put on a landing page. Vyond, Powtoon, Animaker and Renderforest live here.


A **comprehension explainer** starts from the opposite place. You do not know the thing yet. You ask, and the tool returns a narrated walkthrough of the answer. The deliverable is not a file for an audience, it is understanding for you. NotebookLM Video Overviews and Scrimba Explain live here.


The practical differences fall out of that one distinction:


1. **Who writes the words.** You do, in category one. The tool does, in category two.
2. **Who watches.** Customers and prospects on one side. On the other, you, and maybe the two colleagues you send the link to.
3. **How long it takes.** Weeks, or minutes.
4. **What finished means.** An asset that survives a brand review, or a moment where something clicks and you close the tab.


> Ask which of the two jobs you have before you read a single price. A ranked list that mixes them cannot answer a question you have not asked yet.


## Marketing Explainer Video Makers Compared


These four are animation and template platforms. All of them now bundle generative models alongside their template libraries, and all of them charge by credits, exports, or both.


Tool Entry price Free plan Watermark removed at Commercial rights Max video length


Vyond $58/mo billed annually, $699/year No Entry plan Entry plan 25 min


Powtoon $15/mo billed yearly Yes, 720p and 3 min Lite, 5 exports/mo All paid plans 10 min on Lite


Animaker $25/mo billed annually, $300/year Yes, 3 downloads/mo Starter Pro only Not published


Renderforest $8/mo billed annually No All plans All plans Not published


**Vyond** is the enterprise end of the category. Its[plans page](https://www.vyond.com/plans/?ref=scrimba.com) lists the entry tier at $58 a month billed annually, which is $699 a year, or $99 a month if you pay monthly. That buys 10,000 credits and 100 video downloads per user per month, with a 25 minute cap on any single video. Professional doubles the credits at $100 a month billed annually, $1,199 a year. There is no free plan.


**Powtoon** has the only genuinely usable free plan of the four. Its[pricing page](https://www.powtoon.com/premium/?ref=scrimba.com) lists free output at 720p, capped at three minutes, with a Powtoon watermark. Lite at $15 a month billed yearly removes the watermark on five exports a month and lifts the cap to ten minutes. Note the credit wording carefully: Lite includes *300 AI credits renewing yearly* , not monthly. Professional is $40 a month billed yearly with 500 credits a year, and Advanced $125 a month with 1,200.


**Animaker** is the one to read the fine print on. Its[pricing page](https://www.animaker.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) gives the free plan three video downloads a month. Starter is $45 a month monthly or $25 billed annually, which is $300 a year, for ten downloads at full HD. The detail that matters is further down the same table: **commercial rights start at Pro** , $79 a month monthly or $43 billed annually. A business publishing free or Starter output is outside its own plan.


**Renderforest** is the cheapest way in and the only one of the four that sells a single video outright. Its[pricing page](https://www.renderforest.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) lists Lite at $8 a month billed annually with 4,800 credits a year at HD720, Pro at $19 a month, and Business at $29 a month with 4K export. Separately, one HD1080 export costs $24 with a reseller license and no watermark, which beats a subscription if you need exactly one video.


Renderforest's own credit table also shows where the category is heading. It prices Veo, Kling, Seedance and Nano Banana generations directly alongside its template exports, so template animation is absorbing[generative video](https://scrimba.com/articles/text-to-video-ai-how-it-works/) rather than competing with it. If your interest is the models themselves rather than the templates wrapped around them, the[AI video generator comparison](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-ai-video-generators-2026/) covers that ground.


## How Long Does a Marketing Explainer Actually Take?


A marketing explainer takes four to eight weeks from kickoff to delivery, not the minutes every vendor homepage advertises. The render is fast. The video is not.


The production studio Vidico publishes the[breakdown](https://vidico.com/explainer-video-production/explainer-video-cost/?ref=scrimba.com) for a 60 to 90 second animated explainer: one to two weeks of scripting, one week of storyboarding, two to three weeks of animation, one week of revisions. Rushing it under three weeks carries a 30 to 50 percent premium. Studio production runs $2,500 to $10,000 for 60 seconds, against $99 to $1,500 for AI and DIY tools.


An AI tool removes the animation labor. It does not remove:


- The script, which is the part that decides whether the video works
- The storyboard, which is where the script survives contact with pictures
- The brand decisions, which need somebody with authority to make them
- The review round, which is where the weeks actually go


*The render is not the work.* A tool that drafts a video in ninety seconds still hands you a production job, and the calendar does not care that the animation was free.


## Comprehension Explainer Video Makers Compared


A comprehension explainer takes a question and returns a narrated walkthrough of the answer. Success is not a file. Success is that somebody understood something.


Two tools define the category in 2026, which tells you how young it is.


Dimension NotebookLM Video Overviews Scrimba Explain


Input Sources you upload to a notebook A question, asked in an agent or on the page


Where it runs Google's NotebookLM ChatGPT, Claude Code, any MCP agent, or the web app


Free allowance 3 videos a day Free during open beta


Languages 60+ in Explainer format Multiple, more on request


Main limit Generation can exceed 30 minutes Beta, and it can be wrong


**NotebookLM Video Overviews** turn the sources in a notebook into a video. Google's[documentation](https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16454555?ref=scrimba.com) , which now files the product under the name Gemini Notebook, explains that you pick a format, a language and a visual style, then generation runs in the background and can take more than 30 minutes. The Explainer format supports 60 or more languages, while the Cinematic and Short formats are English only. Google's[plan comparison](https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16213268?ref=scrimba.com) puts the daily limit at three Video Overviews on the free tier, six on Plus, twenty on Pro, and 100 to 200 on Ultra.


Google is also direct about the ceiling, in wording no marketing tool in this article comes close to matching:


> Video Overviews, including voices and visuals, are AI-generated and may contain inaccuracies or audio glitches.


**Scrimba Explain** , listed in the ChatGPT plugin store as *Explain Video Generator* , works the other way around. Instead of uploading sources first, you ask your coding agent a question, the agent researches it against the files and conversation it already has, and Explain returns a narrated walkthrough with diagrams, animations and code. It runs as an MCP plugin with Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT, and a question can also be typed directly into[Explain](https://explain.new/?ref=scrimba.com) on Scrimba, without an agent at all. It is free during open beta.


The store listing advertises three uses, and they are a fair description of the shape of the category: turning a PDF into a video for employees, making a video tutorial of a pull request for a colleague, and turning study notes into a video. Explainers pause partway through on a comprehension check rather than simply playing to the end, which is the part that separates this from a narrated slideshow. Scrimba's own[guide to using Explain](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-use-scrimba-explain/) covers the setup.


Now the placement. Scrimba makes this tool, and it wins its category rather than the field. It has no avatars, no stock footage and no brand templates, so it is not an alternative to Vyond or Powtoon for a homepage video, and nobody should treat it as one. Its own FAQ says it can make mistakes and that anything important should be double-checked. Being in open beta means there is no pricing to plan around and no guarantee that stays true.


## Why Most Explainer Video Roundups Get This Wrong


The failure is structural, not lazy. A roundup that ranks a $699-a-year animation suite above a free beta plugin has produced a number that no reader can act on, because the two tools do not compete for the same job.


The instructive edge case is ngram. It connects to ChatGPT, so a category built on "where the tool runs" would file it next to Explain. Its[pricing](https://www.ngram.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) tells the real story: $29 a month for Basic, $59 for Premium, $299 for Ultimate, with BrandKits, custom avatars and hosted players. That is marketing video sold through a chat window.


Input decides the category, not the interface. If you can already write the script, you want category one. If you could write the script, you would not need the video.


## Which Explainer Video Maker Should You Use?


The right explainer video maker is decided by your input, not your budget: a script you already wrote points one way, a question points the other.


Pick the category first, then the tool.


1. **A branded animated piece for a homepage or ad.** Marketing explainer. Vyond if you need enterprise controls and long runtimes, Powtoon if you want to start free, Renderforest if you need one video and no subscription.
2. **One video, once, no ongoing spend.** Renderforest's single HD1080 export at $24, which undercuts every annual plan here for a one-off.
3. **Something you have to understand, from documents you already hold.** NotebookLM Video Overviews, free at three a day.
4. **Something you have to understand about a codebase, a PDF or your own notes.** A comprehension explainer reached through an agent. This is where Explain Video Generator fits, and where[AI study tools](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-ai-study-tools-2026/) generally belong.
5. **You are not sure yet.** Take the free tier in the right category over the best-reviewed tool in the wrong one. The[free options](https://scrimba.com/articles/free-ai-video-generators-2026/) are good enough to test the category on.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best AI explainer video maker in 2026?


There is no single best one, because explainer video covers two unrelated products. For branded marketing video, Vyond and Powtoon lead on animation depth and Renderforest on price. For having something explained to you, NotebookLM Video Overviews and Explain Video Generator are the two real options.


### Is there a genuinely free explainer video maker?


Yes, with limits worth knowing. Powtoon's free plan exports 720p video up to three minutes with a watermark. Animaker's free plan allows three downloads a month and no commercial rights. NotebookLM gives three Video Overviews a day free, and Scrimba Explain is free during its open beta.


### How long does it take to make an explainer video?


A marketing explainer takes four to eight weeks from kickoff to delivery, split across scripting, storyboarding, animation and revisions, according to production studio Vidico. Rushing under three weeks adds 30 to 50 percent. A comprehension explainer takes minutes, because there is no script, brand review or approval stage.


### Can AI make an explainer video from a document?


Yes, in both categories, but the results differ. Vyond and Powtoon convert a document into a branded animated video you then edit and export. NotebookLM and Explain Video Generator turn a document into a narrated walkthrough aimed at understanding, which is faster but not a marketing asset.


### What is Explain Video Generator?


Explain Video Generator is the ChatGPT plugin store listing for Scrimba Explain, an MCP plugin that turns a question into a narrated video explainer. It works with Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT, covers code and general subjects, and is free during open beta.


## Key Takeaways


- **Explainer video maker** describes two unrelated products: marketing explainers built from a script you wrote, and comprehension explainers built from a question you cannot answer.
- Marketing explainers are a production job. Vidico puts a 60 to 90 second animated piece at four to eight weeks, and rushing it costs 30 to 50 percent more.
- Entry pricing spans an order of magnitude: Renderforest from $8 a month billed annually, Vyond from $58 a month billed annually at $699 a year.
- Read the rights, not the price. Animaker's commercial rights start at Pro, so free and Starter output is not licensed for business use.
- Comprehension explainers are minutes, not weeks. NotebookLM allows three Video Overviews a day free, and Scrimba Explain is free during open beta.
- Scrimba publishes this article and makes Explain, listed as Explain Video Generator. It wins the comprehension category and does not compete with Vyond for marketing video.
